harper_lee.name: Harper Lee
harper_lee.biography: Harper Nell Lee was an American novelist best known for her Pulitzer Prize-winning novel To Kill a Mockingbird. Growing up in a small Alabama town during the Great Depression, Lee's experiences deeply influenced her writing about racial injustice and moral courage. She was a close friend of writer Truman Capote and shared his southern Gothic sensibilities. Despite her literary fame, Lee remained private and rarely gave public interviews, living most of her life in her hometown.
harper_lee.literary_style: Narrative storytelling, moral clarity, southern Gothic realism
harper_lee.themes: Racial injustice, morality, coming-of-age, courage, social inequality
major_works: To Kill a Mockingbird (1960) - Pulitzer Prize winner
Go Set a Watchman (2015) - Earlier draft published posthumously
harper_lee.quote: You never really understand a person until you consider things from his point of view.
interesting_facts: Took 10 years to write To Kill a Mockingbird
Only published two novels in her lifetime
Won the Pulitzer Prize at age 35
Inspired by the real-life trial of the Scottsboro Boys

george_orwell.name: George Orwell
george_orwell.biography: Eric Arthur Blair, known by his pen name George Orwell, was a British writer and political commentator. His experiences as colonial police in Burma and his participation in the Spanish Civil War shaped his socialist politics and dystopian fiction. Orwell is celebrated for his clarity of style and his warnings about totalitarianism. He struggled with tuberculosis throughout his life, which ultimately claimed him at just 46 years old.
george_orwell.literary_style: Clear prose, political allegory, dystopian fiction, journalistic realism
george_orwell.themes: Totalitarianism, political corruption, surveillance, truth, freedom of thought
major_works: Animal Farm (1945) - Satirical allegory of Soviet communism
Down and Out in Paris and London (1933)
george_orwell.quote: Freedom is the freedom to say that two plus two make four. If that is granted, all else follows.
interesting_facts: Used a pen name to hide his identity while traveling as a journalist
Served in the Spanish Civil War for the socialist POUM militia
Worked as a colonial police officer in Burma
Wrote about the need for clear, simple English prose

jane_austen.name: Jane Austen
jane_austen.biography: Jane Austen was an English novelist known for her witty social commentary and romantic fiction. Born in the 18th century, she wrote during the Regency era and created some of literature's most beloved characters. Her works examine marriage, social class, and women's limited options with sharp humor and keen observation. Though she achieved little fame during her lifetime, she is now recognized as one of the greatest novelists in English literature.
jane_austen.literary_style: Ironic wit, social satire, romantic comedy, free indirect discourse
jane_austen.themes: Marriage, social class, female agency, love, morality, self-deception
major_works: Pride and Prejudice (1813) - Her most famous novel
awards: Recognized as one of English literature's greatest novelists
jane_austen.quote: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.
interesting_facts: Published under 'A Lady' during her lifetime
Never married, remained close to her family
Wrote letters with sharp wit about contemporary society
Her novels were not widely acclaimed until after her death

arundhati_roy.name: Arundhati Roy
arundhati_roy.biography: Arundhati Roy is an Indian novelist, screenwriter, and political activist. She won the Booker Prize for her debut novel The God of Small Things, which achieved international acclaim. Since then, she has devoted much of her energy to political activism and essays critiquing globalization, nuclear weapons, and social injustice in India. Roy's work is known for its lyrical prose, attention to marginalized voices, and uncompromising political stance.
arundhati_roy.literary_style: Lyrical prose, magical realism, non-linear narrative, poetic imagery
arundhati_roy.themes: Caste oppression, forbidden love, political corruption, environmental destruction, marginalization
major_works: The God of Small Things (1997) - Booker Prize winner
Collections of political essays and speeches
arundhati_roy.quote: To love. To be loved. To never forget your own insignificance.
interesting_facts: First Indian woman to win the Booker Prize
Has written extensively on Kashmir, nuclear weapons, and dams
Known for her fearless critique of Indian government policies
Spent years writing her second novel, published 20 years after her first

salman_rushdie.name: Salman Rushdie
salman_rushdie.biography: Salman Rushdie is a British-Indian novelist and essayist known for his imaginative, often surrealist work blending magic realism with political themes. His novel The Satanic Verses sparked international controversy, forcing him into hiding for years. Despite this, Rushdie continues to write prolifically about migration, identity, and cultural hybridity. He represents postcolonial literature that straddles multiple cultures and challenges literary conventions.
salman_rushdie.literary_style: Magical realism, postcolonial narrative, satirical humor, experimental structure
salman_rushdie.themes: Migration, cultural hybridity, identity, religious critique, historical transformation
major_works: Haroun and the Sea of Stories (1990)
salman_rushdie.quote: What is freedom of expression? Without the freedom to offend, it ceases to exist.
interesting_facts: Lived in hiding for 9 years after The Satanic Verses controversy
Brings together Indian, Islamic, and Western literary traditions
Known for weaving history with magical realism
Has written extensively about migration and cultural displacement

gabriel_garcia_marquez.name: Gabriel García Márquez
gabriel_garcia_marquez.biography: Gabriel García Márquez was a Colombian novelist and journalist, widely regarded as one of the greatest writers of the 20th century. He is best known for pioneering magical realism, blending the fantastical with the mundane in his narratives. His masterpiece, One Hundred Years of Solitude, is considered a cornerstone of Latin American literature. García Márquez's work explores themes of love, memory, and the human condition against backdrops of political turmoil and magical occurrences.
gabriel_garcia_marquez.literary_style: Magical realism, cyclical narrative, lyrical prose, temporal fluidity
gabriel_garcia_marquez.themes: Love and loss, solitude, cyclical time, political violence, family legacy, magic in everyday life
major_works: One Hundred Years of Solitude (1967) - His masterpiece
Love in the Time of Cholera (1985)
gabriel_garcia_marquez.quote: It was as if God had decided to put to the test every capacity for surprise and was keeping the inhabitants of Macondo in a permanent alternation between doubt and revelation.
interesting_facts: Won the Nobel Prize at age 55
Wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude in self-imposed isolation
Worked as a journalist before becoming a novelist
His work revolutionized Latin American literature globally

f_scott_fitzgerald.name: F. Scott Fitzgerald
f_scott_fitzgerald.biography: F. Scott Fitzgerald was an American novelist and short-story writer whose works define the Jazz Age. Fitzgerald captured the disillusionment and excess of the 1920s with elegant prose and complex characters. Though he achieved early success and fame, his later life was marked by personal struggles and financial troubles. His masterpiece, The Great Gatsby, is now considered one of the greatest American novels, though it was not well-received during his lifetime.
f_scott_fitzgerald.literary_style: Lyrical prose, social satire, psychological insight, bildungsroman
f_scott_fitzgerald.themes: The American Dream, wealth and class, love and loss, moral corruption, nostalgia
awards: Recognition as a Great American Novelist
f_scott_fitzgerald.quote: So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.
interesting_facts: Named after Francis Scott Key, author of the National Anthem
The Great Gatsby was considered a commercial failure initially
Died believing himself a failure as a writer
His works are now quintessential American literature

jk_rowling.name: J.K. Rowling
jk_rowling.biography: Joanne Rowling, known as J.K. Rowling, is a British novelist best known for the Harry Potter series, which became a global phenomenon. She conceived the idea for Harry Potter while traveling on a train and wrote the first book while living in poverty as a single mother. Her creation transformed children's literature and has sold over 500 million copies worldwide. Beyond Harry Potter, she has explored adult fiction and continues to be a significant cultural figure.
jk_rowling.literary_style: Fantasy world-building, coming-of-age narrative, mystery elements, character development
jk_rowling.themes: Good vs. evil, friendship, love, courage, prejudice, mortality, acceptance
major_works: The Cormoran Strike series (as Robert Galbraith)
jk_rowling.quote: It is our choices that show what we truly are, far more than our abilities.
interesting_facts: Wrote Harry Potter outline in cafes while watching her daughter
First book rejected by 12 publishers before acceptance
Created an entire magical world with detailed rules and history
Harry Potter books are among the best-selling book series of all time

chinua_achebe.name: Chinua Achebe
chinua_achebe.biography: Chinua Achebe was a Nigerian novelist, poet, and critic, widely regarded as one of Africa's greatest writers. His novel Things Fall Apart challenged Western narratives about Africa and is considered a masterpiece of postcolonial literature. Achebe's work gave voice to African perspectives and indigenous cultures, reframing colonial history. He was deeply committed to African literature and education, working as an editor and promoting African writers globally.
chinua_achebe.literary_style: Narrative realism, proverbs, oral tradition integration, postcolonial critique
chinua_achebe.themes: Colonialism, cultural clash, tradition vs. modernity, individual vs. community, cultural preservation
major_works: Things Fall Apart (1958) - His most famous work
chinua_achebe.quote: If you don't like something, change it. If you can't change it, change the way you think about it.
interesting_facts: Things Fall Apart sold over 10 million copies globally
First African writer to achieve international recognition
Survived a car accident that left him partially paralyzed
Worked to preserve and promote African literature worldwide
